title: Betaretrovirus — mouse mammary tumour and type B/D viruses Coverage Audit
h1: Betaretrovirus — mouse mammary tumour and type B/D viruses
subhead: mouse mammary tumour virus and the type B/D retroviruses
standfirst: Betaretrovirus carries the only separate protease ORF in the family. Where the other three modules fold protease into pol, here pro is its own reading frame between gag and pol, deposited 94 times. The module also carries Rem, an RNA export protein the deposited vocabulary never names once.

sections.title: What the module calls
sections.lede: Four profiled features plus a spliced regulator with no deposited vocabulary at all.

blocks.html: pro is declared on evidence, not convention: testing the module's own naming rules before the generic subunit rule is what kept its 94 deposits together. Treating “protease” as a pol cleavage product — which it is in the other three modules — would have cut the collection to a quarter of its evidence. REM is called by get_splice_variant_features.pl from references whose coding sequence crosses one intron; it never takes copy_num.

sections.title: Where it does not call, and why

blocks.html: REM's overall rate is low and the denominator is the reason. Rem exists in the MMTV clade and nowhere else in the genus, and it fires in every MMTV-group genome of the held-out panel — 100% inside the clade. Its overlap with ENV is real MMTV architecture, since rem shares the envelope signal-peptide exon, and is declared expected rather than suppressed. REM is also the clearest case in this family of a feature the strings could never have found: zero deposits anywhere in the genus name it.

GAG, POL and ENV carry copy_num on biology, not on their rates: every replication-competent retrovirus encodes gag, pol and env, so a genome without one is defective and is flagged as missing an essential feature. That flag is true rather than false only if the genomes it lands on really lack the gene, so each of the 27 exemplars without an ENV call was searched by tblastn against the full ENV collection (a called genome, 1051323.3, scores 1175 bits over 100% of an envelope protein). 26 of 27 carry no intact env: 25 have one interrupted by stop codons or frameshifts and 1 has no envelope sequence at all. The other one carries an intact env the profiles do not call (3386024.3 at 1419 bits) — a recall gap in the module, not in the genome, and the quality flag on it is wrong.

94.8% of the 574 deposited features from this module's taxa are bound by a naming rule. The remainder are recorded in UNASSIGNED and DISCARDED: the first is vocabulary no rule reached, the second is records the source itself calls partial or truncated, which the project discards rather than trains on.

sections.title: Vocabulary saturation
sections.lede: How fast each vocabulary stops growing as genomes are added.

blocks.html: The deposited vocabulary keeps growing; the module's does not. At the depth both reach, 38.8 distinct source strings correspond to 5.0 controlled annotations, a 7.8-fold collapse. The module reaches 95% of its final vocabulary after 52 proteins against the source's 259.

Coverage is measured by annotating genomes through the real GTO pipeline — annotate_by_viral_pssm-GTO.pl, then the transcript-edit and splice passes, then viral_genome_quality.pl — not by a reimplementation. Spliced features are included, which the flat feature-table path cannot represent. Exemplars are clustered at 95% nucleotide identity over 90% of length, so one row is one distinct sequence rather than one deposit: this module's 145 genomes reduce to 53 exemplars, and without that step a rate would report how often a sequence was deposited rather than how often the module calls it. Call rates are taken over the 52 of 53 exemplars this module actually claimed; an unrouted genome contributes no features and counting it would understate every rate, and this is the same denominator the evaluation and the copy_num decisions used.

source_note: Measured 27 October 2026 from the shipped module: the Betaretrovirus block of Viral_PSSM.json, its profiles and collections, and the 27 October coverage annotation over 53 exemplars de-replicated from 145 genomes. Vocabulary figures come from collections/synonyms.tsv, written by the module's own builder from the naming rules, and count deposited features rather than unique sequences.
